newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Sing Heng Chan appeal rejected by SC.
newsitem.headline: Sing Heng Chan appeal rejected by SC.

text.p: Sin Heng Chan (Malaya) Bhd (SHC) said that the Securities Commission has rejected its appeal to reconsider a planned acquisition of a British gaming firm and a special share issue.

A statement sent by the feedmiller to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange on Tuesday said the plan was rejected as it did not comply with a ruling which requires non-complementary businesses injected into a listed company to show reasonable profits for the past three years.
SHC, in its earlier application, appealed that this requirement be waived.

The proposed acquisition subject, Stenworld Ltd, has a 90 percent stake in Pascal & Co, which in turn has a 20-year contract from November 1994 to operate the British National Hospital Trust Lotteries.
The securities watchdog also rejected a planned issue of 70 million new shares for Bumiputera (ethnic Malay) shareholders to Macronet Sdn Bhd, a SHC shareholder.
Both proposals were part of a restructuring and rescue scheme which included a rights issue, another proposed acquisition and an employee share option scheme.
SHC said it is considering alternative businesses to be injected into it to strengthen and broaden the earnings and assets bases of the group.
Meanwhile, the stock exchange said in an announcement that SHC shares will be requoted on Thursday.
The stock was suspended from July 22 with the last trading price at 48.75 ringgit.
